Knowledge transfer · User manual · Reconstructed from the source code, October 2026

HEA Digital Safety Tools (MTE)

How the electronic Permit-To-Work system works: who uses it, what each screen is for, and what happens behind every button.

Executive summary

HEA Digital Safety Tools (MTE) is Hitachi Elevator Asia's internal web application. It replaces paper safety forms used on lift (elevator) and escalator installation and maintenance sites. Before and during work at a building, field teams fill in safety records on a phone, tablet or PC. Supervisors and managers then review and approve those records on screen. Every record keeps:

  • who did what, and when
  • the GPS location it was filled in from
  • any photos or PDFs attached as evidence

Why it exists

Singapore workplace-safety rules (the WSH Act, MOM, HDB, SCDF and others) require documented proof that work at height, lifting and lift-shaft work was planned, briefed and checked. Paper forms are slow to route, easy to lose and hard to audit. This system makes each form electronic, routes it to the right reviewer, and stores a permanent, searchable history.

Who uses it

Field technicians and team leaders (from HEA and its subcontractors) fill in forms. Assessors, HEA Safety officers and Project Managers review and approve them. Administrators maintain users, teams, contractors and equipment lists. Management uses the dashboards and reports to see activity and manpower on site.

The four safety records at the heart of the system

1. Permit To Work (PTW) for work at height

Formal written permission before anyone works at height. It is checked by up to three reviewers (WAH Assessor → HEA Safety → Project Manager), then reviewed every day while the work runs, and finally closed. It lasts at most 7 days.

Open the PTW guide →

2. Toolbox Meeting (TBM)

The short daily safety briefing a team leader gives before work starts. It records who attended, the hazards discussed and the units being worked on. The team's named approver receives an email and endorses it. TBM attendance also feeds the "Manpower at Site" chart.

Open the TBM guide →

3. Safety Action Key Points Checklist

A per-job checklist for elevator or escalator work. The team leader ticks every key safety point (or marks a whole section "Not applicable") and signs four personal-responsibility declarations. An approver then signs it off.

Open the Checklist guide →

4. Compliance Confirmation Point (CCP)

Proof, with photos, that the required control measures were in place before a key activity started, such as "Maintenance Work" or "Hoisting of lift cage". A CCP Approver approves, returns or rejects it, and a monitoring report tracks it across all buildings.

Open the CCP guide →

How everything connects: the high-level business process

Administrators first set up the "master data": users, contractors, teams and equipment. Everyday users then sign in, choose the team they are working with, and create safety records against that team's equipment. Each record travels through a review chain. Dashboards and reports summarise the results.

Common rules that apply to every safety record

Nothing saves until Submit

A new form exists only on your screen until you press Submit. There is no "save draft". If you close the browser or your session ends first, the work is lost.

Everything belongs to a team

Every record is filed under the team you selected after signing in. To work on another team's records you must use Change Team.

Location is captured

The browser asks to share your location. The latitude and longitude appear at the bottom of the form and are stored with the record as evidence of where it was filled in.

Return vs Reject

Return sends a record back to its creator to fix and resubmit. Reject is final: the record can never be reopened. Both need a written reason.

Attachments

Photos (.jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .png) and PDFs up to 4 MB each. They are attached to the record only when you press Submit.

Your name is your signature

There are no drawn signatures. When you press Submit, Verify or Approve, the system stamps your name, job title (designation) and company onto the record with the date and time.

Getting started: signing in, choosing a team and finding your way around

Every user goes through the same three steps before they can do anything: sign in → choose a team → use the menu. This tab explains each step and the screen layout.

Feature overview: why sign-in and team selection exist

What it does: Sign-in identifies you, so the system can stamp your name on everything you do and show you only the menus and records your role allows. Team selection tells the system which crew or site you are working with today, so every list, dropdown and new record is filtered to that team.

Why it was built this way: One person (for example a supervisor) may cover several teams. Rather than mixing every team's permits together, the system makes you pick one team at a time, much like choosing which project folder to open.

Who uses it: Everyone.

Key terminology
User ID
Your email address. It is set automatically when an administrator creates your account.
Team
A working group or site that records belong to (for example "Team M1"). Older screens and the database call it a "Project". The Select Team screen even labels the team name column "Building Name". It is the same thing.
Main Contractor
The company that owns a team (usually HEA). Staff of the main contractor get wider visibility of that team's permits.
Left menu
The navigation list on the left. Its items depend on your roles.
Configuration panel
A second menu on the right, holding the administration and setup screens your role allows.
CAPTCHA
The short number code you type on the sign-in page to prove you are a person and not an automated program.

That account held almost every role, so other users may see fewer items. The menu is stored in the database and may differ slightly on the live system. The list pages (for example "Permit To Work List") did not appear as menu items for that account; users land on them after pressing Submit.
Changing your own password

There is no "Forgot password" link on the sign-in page. To change your password once you are signed in:

  1. Open User Management from the Configuration panel. Ordinary users see only their own record there.
  2. Click Edit on your own row. Only when you edit your own record do two extra boxes appear: Password and Confirm.
  3. Type the new password twice and click Update. If the two entries differ you see "Please enter the valid password." Leaving both blank keeps your current password.

If you have forgotten your password, ask an administrator to click Reset Password on your account. A new random 8-character password is emailed to you (subject "Reset Password").

Passwords can be at most 20 characters long.
Common pitfalls and edge cases
  • "Invalid login attempt." means the User ID or password is wrong. The User ID is your full email address. Passwords are case-sensitive.
  • CAPTCHA keeps failing: use the refresh arrow to get a clearer code. Only digits 1–9 are used, never 0.
  • No lockout: the system does not lock your account after failed attempts. Repeated failures are not a reason an account stops working.
  • The team I need isn't listed: you are not on that team's staff list and your company isn't its main contractor. Ask an administrator to add you under Administration → Project Configuration → "2. Manpower & Staff".
  • Suddenly sent back to "Select the Team": the team you were working in was deleted or renamed by an administrator while you were signed in. Choose it again under its new name.
  • Suddenly sent back to the sign-in page: your session ended, or a form failed to load. Sign in again. Anything you had not submitted is lost.
  • The "Register" page: it exists but does nothing. New accounts can only be created by an administrator.

Permit To Work (PTW): work at height

An electronic permit that must be fully approved before anyone works at height on a lift or escalator job. It runs through three sign-offs, a daily check while the work is under way, a completion notice and a closure review.

Feature overview and plain-English purpose

What it does: A worker (the applicant) asks for permission to carry out a specific job at height. The request covers:

  • one team
  • one piece of equipment, chosen by its manufacturing (MFG) number
  • a period of 1 to 7 days
  • a number of workers

The applicant answers a safety checklist that matches the type of work and attaches photos or documents as evidence. The permit then passes through:

  1. WAH Assessor (Working-At-Height assessor): endorses that the work matches the risk assessment and safe work practices.
  2. HEA Safety: confirms they are satisfied with the safety provisions.
  3. HEA Project Manager / Authorised Competent Person: gives final approval. Only now may work begin.
  4. Daily review: on each permitted day the applicant and an assessor tick that day off.
  5. Completion notice: the applicant declares the work finished.
  6. Closure review: the main contractor acknowledges completion.

Why it was built: Singapore law and HEA's own Safety & Health Management System require a written permit for work at height. The electronic version enforces the order of sign-offs, records who approved what and when, and gives auditors a complete history.

What problem it solves: No more paper permits lost between site and office. Approvers see waiting permits in one Pending list. A permit can be revoked instantly if a safety lapse is found.

What happens if a step fails: If a reviewer is not satisfied, they either return the permit (the applicant fixes it and the whole chain starts again) or reject it (it is closed for good and a new permit must be raised). If work is unsafe after approval, the permit can be revoked, which ends it immediately.

Important: The PTW module sends no email notifications. Each reviewer must open their Pending list regularly to see permits waiting for them.
Key terminology
PTW
Permit To Work.
WAH
Working At Height.
Applicant
The person who raises the permit. Their name, designation and company are stamped in "Part 1".
Manufacturing Number (MFG No.)
The identifying number of the lift or escalator unit the work is on. It is chosen from the team's list of active equipment.
Work Type
The category of work. Each work type has its own checklist of safety questions (set up by administrators as a "template").
Total Worker
How many people will do the work (1 to 1000).
Parts 1–7
The sections of the permit form, one per stage of the life cycle (described below).
Endorse / Verify / Approve
The three review actions, by the Assessor, HEA Safety and the Project Manager respectively.
Daily Review
A tick for each day of the permit, given by the applicant and by an assessor, showing that day's work was checked.
Return
Send back to the applicant for correction. The permit can be edited and resubmitted.
Reject
Refuse permanently. The permit is closed and read-only.
Revoke
Cancel an already approved permit, for example after a safety lapse. Final.
Closure Review
The final acknowledgement by the main contractor that the work is complete.
Main contractor
The company that owns the team. Some reviewer steps are only visible to main-contractor staff.

Every Part shows the person's Name, Designation and Company, plus a Remarks box. At the bottom of the form are the reason box "For Return, Reject & Revoke : Please specify the reason" and the line "Location : Latitude …, Longitude …".

The six permit conditions printed on every permit

  1. Applicant(s) shall comply with WSH Act, WSH Subsidiary Legislations, NEA Legislations, Code of Practices etc.
  2. Permit-To-Work is to be submitted 3 working days in advance (minimum) & PTW-maximum period is 7 days and non-automatic renewal and to resubmit PTW for approval. Daily Permit-To-Work shall apply which applicable.
  3. Permit-To-Work is to be approval by Project Manager before commence of work & submit minimum 3 days in advance.
  4. Approved PTW to be displayed prominently at where the working at height is to be carried out, e.g. Access Point.
  5. Workers must have complete CSOC & Safety Induction & to adhere with HEA Safety & Health Management System (SHMS), Safe Work Practices (SWP) and comply with all relevant Occupational Safety & Health (OSH) legislations including MOM, NEA, HDB, SCDF etc.
  6. PTW will be revoked & shall be considered invalid if any safety non-compliance/lapse is found & communicated.
The "3 working days in advance" rule is printed but not enforced. The system only checks that the start date is today or later.

Step-by-step journey C: fixing a returned permit (Applicant)
1

Step 1: Find the returned permit

Open the Permit To Work List. The card shows RETURNED. Click Details.

📷 What to look at
Screen
/PTW/NewPTW.aspx?Status=D, title "Permit To Work - Returned"
Highlight
The read-only reason at the bottom, and the editable fields at the top.
Sample data
Reason shown: "Rescue plan not attached. Please upload RP-07 and resubmit."
2

Step 2: Correct and resubmit

Make the changes (for example upload the missing file). If the original start date is now in the past, move the dates forward. Then click Submit.

Behind the scenes: All earlier review stamps (Parts 2–4) and daily review rows are cleared, and the permit restarts at SUBMITTED. The assessor, safety officer and Project Manager must all sign again.
Only the person who originally raised the permit can resubmit it. Avoid changing the Work Type on a returned permit: the old checklist answers are kept as well as the new questions, which duplicates the checklist.
Step-by-step journey D: daily review, completion and closure
1

Step 1: Daily review (each permit day)

While the permit is APPROVED, Part 5 shows one row per day, for example "Day 2 (06/10/26)". Each row has two halves:

  • Applicant (opens the permit from the Permit To Work List): optional remark, then Verify.
  • Assessor (opens it from Pending): optional remark, then Verify. This also ticks the applicant half if it was left blank.
📷 What to look at
Screen
/PTW/NewPTW.aspx, Part 5 "Daily Review by WAH Supervisor or Above"
Highlight
The "Day 2 (06/10/26)" row: Applicant tick, remark and Verify; Assessor tick, remark and Verify.
Sample data
Applicant remark: "Lifeline checked 08:05, all 4 workers harnessed." · Assessor remark: "Site visit OK."
A day's Verify button only works on that day or the following day. Missed days cannot be ticked later. Daily ticks are recorded for audit but are not required before completion.
2

Step 2: Revoke, if something goes wrong

Toolbox Meeting (TBM)

The daily pre-work safety briefing. A team leader records the briefing, the attendees, the hazards discussed and the units being worked on. The team's named TBM approver is emailed and endorses it.

Feature overview and plain-English purpose

What it does: Before work starts each morning (or afternoon), the team leader runs a short "toolbox talk". The TBM form captures:

  • the date, and whether it was the AM or PM session (one only)
  • confirmation of 10 standard briefing items, such as the health check, PPE check and barricades
  • who attended
  • each hazard or issue discussed, with the possible accident, the countermeasure and the team's action goal
  • which lift or escalator units the team will work on
  • optional photos or PDFs

On Submit, an email goes to the team's assigned TBM approver, who endorses (approves), returns or rejects the record.

Why it was built: Daily briefings are a key safety control and a regulatory expectation. Recording them electronically proves each briefing happened, shows who was present, and builds a reliable daily headcount.

Second purpose: manpower tracking. TBM attendance is the only source for the "Manpower at Site" chart on the Overview page and for the all-teams "TBM Report". If teams skip their TBM, the manpower figures will under-count.

What happens if a step fails: If the team has no valid approver, the TBM cannot be submitted at all (see pitfalls). If the approver returns it, the team leader corrects it and resubmits. If it is rejected, it is closed for good.

Key terminology
TBM
Toolbox Meeting: the daily pre-work safety briefing.
Conducted By
The person who created and submitted the TBM (the team leader).
Work Description (AM / PM)
What the team will do in that session. Exactly one of the two must be filled in; this decides whether the TBM counts as a morning or an afternoon session.
Briefing items
The 10 standard topics the leader must cover, each answered from a dropdown (normally Yes / No / NA).
Attendee
A worker present at the briefing, chosen from users of your own company.
Hazard / Issue Record
One topic discussed: Topics Discussed, Possible Hazard, Possible Accident, Countermeasure/counteraction, Today's Team Action Goal and Feedback.
Unit No / Manufacturing Number
The lift or escalator units being worked on, chosen from the team's active equipment, with the machine type (Elevator or Escalator).
TBM Approver
One named person per team, set by an administrator in Team Management. They receive the email and endorse the team's TBMs. They must hold the PTW APPROVER role and have an email address.
Endorsement
The approver's approval block: name, designation, company and remarks.
Life cycle of a Toolbox Meeting 
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  [*] --> New: Team leader opens New TBM
  New --> Submitted: Submit (email sent to team TBM approver)
  Submitted --> Approved: Approver - Approve
  Submitted --> Returned: Approver - Return + reason
  Submitted --> Rejected: Approver - Reject + reason
  Returned --> Submitted: Creator edits and resubmits (new email)
  Approved --> [*]
  Rejected --> [*]
StatusMeaning
NEWBeing filled in. Not saved yet.
SUBMITTEDWaiting for the team's TBM approver. An email has been sent.
APPROVEDEndorsed by the approver. Final.
RETURNEDSent back with a reason. The creator can edit it and submit again.
REJECTEDRefused. Final.
Screen guide: the three TBM screens
ScreenAddressWhat it is for
TBM form ("Toolbox Meeting - New / Submitted / …")/TBM/NewTBM.aspxCreate, view, approve, return or reject a TBM
"Toolbox Meeting List"/TBM/MyTBM.aspxAll TBMs of the current team, newest first. Each card shows the date, who conducted it, the AM and PM descriptions, the status and a Details button.
"Toolbox Meeting - Pending"/TBM/PendingTBM.aspxSubmitted TBMs waiting for you (team approver or admin). Each card has a Verify button.

The 10 standard briefing items

Shown under the heading Please carry out items briefing and select "Yes" after it is done. :-

  1. Health check (Eg: Are you OK to work ? Any Fatigue ?)
  2. PPE Check (Eg: Attire, Safety Shoes, Safety Harness, Safety Belt, Helmet c/w chin strap, Hand Gloves etc).
  3. Set-up barricades and signages before start work.
  4. Use of proper tools & instruments for suitable equipment.
  5. No drinks, food and smoking within premises.
  6. Maintain proper housekeeping.
  7. Safety driving / riding habit complying to traffic regulations
  8. Safety ownership, authority to stop work and report near miss / hazard to supervisor.
  9. Operation key must pass to team leader before start of ES work.
  10. Others : Access to Private Lobby is Strictly Prohibited without Approval from Building Owner.

Safety Action Key Points Checklist

A per-job checklist for elevator and escalator work. The team leader ticks every key safety point for the machine type, or marks whole sections "Not applicable", and signs four personal-responsibility declarations. Any PTW Approver can sign it off.

Feature overview and plain-English purpose

What it does: The team leader names themselves and a co-worker, picks the units to be worked on, and the system generates the right checklist:

  • an Elevator checklist
  • an Escalator checklist
  • both, if units of both kinds are added

The checklist is grouped into sections such as working at height, landing doors, car operation, hoisting, live electrical parts and confined spaces. Each applicable item must be ticked. A section that doesn't apply to today's job is marked "Not applicable", which greys out its items. Four confirmation statements make the leader personally accountable for briefing, supervising, stopping unsafe work and finishing safely.

Why it was built: It mirrors HEA's "Key Points Confirmation Sheet" so that the critical controls for each type of lift work are consciously checked before every job, and so the person in charge accepts responsibility in writing.

What happens if a step fails: Submit is refused until equipment is added, every mandatory section is ticked or marked Not applicable, and all four confirmations are ticked. An approver can return the checklist for correction or reject it.

The Checklist sends no email. Approvers must check their Pending list.
Key terminology
Key Points
The critical safety controls for a type of lift or escalator work.
Team leader / Co-worker
The two names typed at the top of the form (up to 100 characters each).
Checklist Date
The date of the job: any past date up to tomorrow.
Building Name & EL/ES No.
How a unit is identified: the building plus the lift (EL) or escalator (ES) number, for example "Blk 789 Jurong West St 71 L3".
MFG No.
The unit's manufacturing number, filled in automatically.
Machine Type
Elevator or Escalator. It decides which checklist appears.
Section heading tick
A bold tick box that confirms a whole section.
Not applicable
A tick beside certain section headings. It marks the whole section as not relevant today and disables its items.
Applicant Details / confirmations
The four declarations the team leader must tick before submitting.
Life cycle of a Checklist 
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  [*] --> New: Team leader opens New Checklist
  New --> Submitted: Submit (all checks pass)
  Submitted --> Approved: PTW Approver / Admin - Approve
  Submitted --> Returned: Return + reason
  Submitted --> Rejected: Reject + reason
  Returned --> Submitted: Creator edits and resubmits
  Approved --> [*]
  Rejected --> [*]

Statuses are the same as for TBM: NEW SUBMITTED APPROVED RETURNED REJECTED. Page titles read "Safety Action Key Points Checklist - New / Submitted / Approved / Returned / Rejected".

Screen guide
ScreenAddressWhat it is for
Checklist form/Checklist/NewChecklist.aspxCreate, view, approve, return or reject
"Safety Action Key Points Checklist" (list)/Checklist/MyChecklist.aspxAll checklists of the selected team, newest first, each with a Details button
"Safety Action Key Points Checklist - Pending"/Checklist/PendingChecklist.aspxSubmitted checklists awaiting approval, each with a Verify button

The four confirmations (all must be ticked)

Introduced by: "I will ensure that the check items specified in the Key Points Confirmation Sheet are thoroughly implemented, and I will fulfill my responsibilities as the person in-charge of the work as outlined below." followed by "Check each box below for confirmation:"

  1. Before start of work, I have explained and provided instructions on the specific details of the day's work location, work content and procedures, worker assignments and roles, as well as potential hazards and countermeasures. I will also confirm that all team members have understood these points before starting the work.
  2. During the work, I will supervise and ensure that all personnel confirm their safety at all times before proceeding to the next action.
  3. If the work cannot be carried out safely, I will suspend the work and ensure that it is reported to my supervisor (line manager).
  4. I will ensure that no one is exposed to danger and that the work is completed safely from start to finish.

Sections that offer "Not applicable"

Section headings about any of these topics get a "Not applicable" tick: working at height · landing / hall doors · car operation · driving operation · moving platform · multiple workers · hoisting machines · horizontal pulling of heavy loads · control panels / live parts · moving / rotating parts · electric tools · confined spaces · organic solvents.

Items that are always mandatory

Items about a less-experienced worker with under one year, the safety check of on-site movement routes, if a worker feels unwell, and unplanned work must always be ticked. If the template does not contain these sentences, the first four items under "Common Compliance Requirements" must be ticked instead.

Compliance Confirmation Point (CCP)

Photo-backed proof that the required control measures were in place before a key activity (such as "Maintenance Work" or "Hoisting of lift cage") started at a building. A CCP Approver endorses it, and a monitoring report tracks CCPs across all buildings.

Feature overview and plain-English purpose

What it does: At a critical point in an installation or maintenance job, the team records:

  • the team leader and co-worker
  • the building and lift
  • the key activity and the date
  • an answer for each "Control Measures Implemented" question for that activity
  • photos or PDFs as evidence

A CCP Approver then reviews it and approves (marks it COMPLETED), returns it for correction, or rejects it.

Why it was built: Some activities, such as hoisting a lift cage, are dangerous enough that management wants confirmed, evidenced controls before work proceeds. The monitoring report lets HQ see at a glance which buildings have had which activities confirmed.

Name note: The forms and menu say Compliance Confirmation Point. The Overview chart still uses the older name Compliance Check Point. Both mean the same thing.

CCP sends no email. Approvers must check "Pending Approval".
Key terminology
CCP
Compliance Confirmation Point.
Key Activities
The activity being confirmed. The system always offers "Maintenance Work" and "Hoisting of lift cage", plus any other active activities an administrator has set up.
Control Measures Implemented
The question list for the chosen activity. Each question has a dropdown answer (for example Yes / No / NA).
Building Name
The unit being worked on, shown as "Building Name" plus "EL/ES No.", for example "Blk 123 Tampines St 11 L2".
Endorsement
The approver's block: Name, "CCP Approver", Designation, Company Name.
COMPLETED
The CCP list's word for an approved CCP. The Overview chart calls the same status "Approved".

  Submitted --> Returned: Return + reason
  Submitted --> Rejected: Reject + reason
  Returned --> Submitted: Creator edits and resubmits
  Returned --> Deleted: Creator - Delete
  Completed --> [*]
  Rejected --> [*]
  Deleted --> [*]
StatusMeaning
NEWBeing filled in. Not saved.
SUBMITTEDWaiting for a CCP Approver
COMPLETEDApproved. Final.
RETURNEDSent back. The creator can fix and resubmit, or delete it.
REJECTEDRefused. Final.
DELETEDWithdrawn by the creator after a return. It still appears in lists, marked DELETED.

Step-by-step journey C: handling a returned CCP (Creator)
1

Step 1: Fix and resubmit, or delete

Open the CCP list and click Details on the RETURNED CCP. The reason is shown. Then:

  • edit the fields, answers or attachments and click Submit, or
  • click Delete to withdraw it (it becomes DELETED), or
  • click Cancel to leave without changes.
Avoid changing the Key Activity on a returned CCP: the old answers are kept as well as the new questions.
Common pitfalls and edge cases
MessageCause / fix
"Please enter the Team leader name" / "Please enter the Co-worker name"Both names are required
"Please select the Building Name"Choose a unit. If the list is empty, the team has no active equipment.
"Please select the Key Activities"Choose an activity
"Please select the Date"Pick a date
"Please select the Answer."A control-measure question is unanswered
"Please enter the Reason"Return or Reject was clicked without a reason
"File size exceeds the maximum allowed size, which is 4MB." / "The selected file is not allowed."File too big or the wrong type
Submit or Approve does nothingA hidden save error occurred. Report it with the time and building.
  • Only the creator sees and can edit a RETURNED CCP. Other users see it read-only, without the reason or attachments.
  • An Admin without the CCP APPROVER role sees an empty Pending list, but can still approve by opening the CCP from the list.
  • The lists are loaded when you open the page. Re-open the page from the menu to refresh it.

Dashboards & reports

Where managers see activity and manpower: the team Overview dashboard, the all-teams TBM Report, the CCP Project Monitoring report, and the per-permit PDF.

Team Overview dashboard

What it is: The landing page after you select a team (/ProjectOverview.aspx, header "Overview (Team M1)"). It shows:

  • Team information: photo, name, address, description, main contractor and contact line, for example "Mr Lee (Number : 6123 4567)".
  • Three doughnut charts counting this team's records by status, with legend "Status (count)" and labels "percent (count)":
    • "Permit To Work"
    • "Toobox Meeting" (misspelled on screen)
    • "Compliance Check Point"
  • "Manpower at Site" bar chart: for each of the last 9 days, one bar per company showing how many people attended Toolbox Meetings. A person counts 0.5 per session, so someone at both the AM and PM TBM counts as 1.
  • Manpower details grid below the chart: Applied Date, Company Name, Applicant Name, Job Designation and Session (AM/PM), for all dates, grouped by date, with filters and Export to XLSX.
📷 What to look at
Screen
/ProjectOverview.aspx
Highlight
The three charts, the Manpower at Site chart with two company series, and the Export to XLSX button on the details grid.
Sample data
PTW: Approved 12, Submitted 3, Closed 20 · Manpower 05-Oct-2026: Hitachi Elevator Asia 6.0, Lift Pro Engineering 3.5
Manpower figures come only from submitted or approved Toolbox Meetings. Workers not recorded in a TBM are not counted. The charts can be rotated with the mouse (3D).
TBM Report (all teams)

Where: /Settings/TBMReportAll.aspx, title "TBM Report", normally reached from the Configuration panel.

What it shows: one row per person per Toolbox Meeting, for every team. That means the leader who conducted the TBM plus each attendee, for TBMs that are submitted or approved. Columns:

  • Applied Date (newest first)
  • Project Name (the team)
  • Company Name
  • Applicant Name
  • Job Designation
  • MFG No: the units, comma-separated, or "(No MFG Selected)"
  • Session (AM/PM)

How to use it: drag a column header into the group area to group (for example by Company Name), use the column filter buttons, read the counts in the footer, and click Export to XLSX to download for Excel.

TBM and Checklist reports were switched off.

Document List (hidden from the menu)

Where: /DocumentManagement.aspx, title "Document List". The menu entry is deliberately hidden, but the page still works if you know the address.

Purpose: a simple library of documents per team, such as method statements and certificates. Each document has a Document Type (from the Document Type setting), a Title and a file.

  1. New opens a form. Choose the Document Type, type a Title, upload the file, and click Update.
  2. To change a document, click its row, then click Edit.
  3. Click Download on a row to get the file.

Messages you may see:

  • "Please select the Document Type."
  • "Please enter the Equipment Description." (this actually refers to the Title)
  • "Please select and upload the Document."

There is no Delete. Team names longer than 20 characters may cause documents to go missing (see Known Issues).

Administration: setting up users, teams, contractors and equipment

The "master data" every form depends on. If a dropdown is empty or someone can't see a team, the fix is almost always on one of these screens. Equipment Management is in the left menu; the other setup screens are opened from the Configuration panel on the right.

How the master data fits together 
flowchart LR
  CON["Contractor<br/>e.g. Hitachi Elevator Asia,<br/>Lift Pro Engineering"] -->|employs| USR["User<br/>email = User ID<br/>role bundle"]
  CON -->|is main contractor of| TEAM["Team<br/>e.g. Team M1"]
  USR -->|named as TBM Approver| TEAM
  TEAM -->|owns| EQ["Equipment<br/>Building Name, EL/ES No., MFG No."]
  TEAM -->|Project Configuration:<br/>extra contractors and staff| USR
  EQ --> FORMS["PTW · TBM · Checklist · CCP"]
  TEAM --> FORMS
  USR --> FORMS
  • Every user belongs to exactly one contractor (company).
  • Every team has one main contractor and one TBM approver.
  • Every piece of equipment belongs to one team. Only active equipment appears in the forms.
  • Project Configuration adds extra contractors and individual staff to a team. Adding someone as staff is what lets them select a team their own company doesn't own.

Recommended order when onboarding a new site

  1. Create the subcontractor in Contractor List if it is new.
  2. Create the users in User Management (one at a time, or with Upload Excel).
  3. Create the team in Team Management and choose its TBM Approver.
  4. Add subcontractor staff to the team in Project Configuration → 2. Manpower & Staff.
  5. Select the team, then add its lifts and escalators in Equipment List.

3

Step 3 (optional): Import many users from Excel

Click Upload Excel and choose an .xlsx or .xlsm file (up to 10 MB).

  • Row 1 must contain exactly these headings: Title, First Name, Last Name, Document Type, Document No, Contact No, Email Address, Contractor Name, Position, User Roles.
  • User Roles must be Applicant, Approver or Admin (comma-separated).
  • Existing email addresses are updated; new ones are created and emailed a password.

On success you see "Import successful. N row(s) added and M row(s) updated." If anything is wrong, a table titled "Import Incomplete: Issues Detected" lists each Row, Field, Issue and Suggested Fix, for example "Unknown Contractor Name (Liftpro)" or "Use NRIC, FIN, or WP."

Other actions

  • Reset Password: asks "Confirm Reset the Account, the Password will send thru email ?" and then emails a new password.
  • Delete: asks "Are you sure you want to proceed?" and then permanently removes the user and their roles. A copy is kept in a history table. Their past records keep their name.
  • Edit: change any field. Changing the role bundle replaces all of the person's roles.

Messages

"Please select the Title." · "Please enter the First Name." · "Please enter the Last Name." · "Please select the Document Type." · "Please enter the Document Number." · "Please enter the Contact Number." · "Please enter the Email Address." · "The Email has been registered." · "Please select the Constructor." · "Please enter the Position." · "Please select the User Role." · "Only Applicant, Approver, and Admin roles are allowed."

Be careful:
  • Changing a user's email address creates a second, new account and emails it a password. The old account remains. Delete the old one if that was the intention.
  • There is no "lock" for users, only delete.

Who sees whom: Application Admins see all users. Company Admins see only their own company's users. Everyone else sees only themselves (and can only Edit).

Roles & permissions

Administrators assign one of three easy bundles. Behind each bundle the system grants several detailed roles, and those detailed roles drive the menus, the Pending lists and the approval buttons.

The three role bundles (what admins choose)
BundleTypical personDetailed roles granted
ApplicantTechnician, team leader, subcontractor supervisorPTW USER, TBM USER, CCP USER, CKL USER
ApproverWAH assessor, HEA safety officer, project manager, site supervisorPTW ASSESSOR, PTW SAFETY, PTW APPROVER, PTW CLOSURE, CCP APPROVER
AdminSystem administrator, HQ safety leadAll 11 roles, including APPLICATION ADMIN and COMPANY ADMIN
Things to know:
  • The Approver bundle does not include the Applicant roles. An approver who also raises permits needs both bundles ticked.
  • Ticking Admin overrides the others.
  • Because one bundle grants all four PTW reviewer roles, the system cannot separate "assessor-only" from "approver-only" people. Separation of duties depends on site practice.

The left-menu items each role sees are configured in the database, not in the program. This matrix describes what the system allows. Whether the menu link is visible depends on that configuration.

The 11 detailed roles (reference)
Role namePlain meaning
PTW USERCan raise Permits To Work
TBM USERCan record Toolbox Meetings

CCP USERCan record Compliance Confirmation Points
PTW ASSESSORWAH Assessor: endorses permits (Part 2), does daily reviews, can revoke

COMPANY ADMINAdministrator for their own company only. Note: anywhere the system checks "is this an admin", Company Admins also count.
The "main contractor" rule

Each team has one main contractor (normally HEA). Users who work for the main contractor get a wider view of PTWs:

  • They see all of the team's permits in the Permit To Work List. Subcontractor reviewers see only their own company's.
  • Only main-contractor PTW Approvers see permits waiting for final approval in Pending.
  • Only main-contractor reviewers see approved permits in Pending (for daily review and revoke).

Example: Ms Ong of Lift Pro Engineering holds the Approver bundle. On Team M1 (main contractor HEA) she can endorse her own company's permits as Assessor. She will never see permits waiting for Project Manager approval. Those go only to HEA's approvers.

Global glossary & status reference

On screen, the system shows statuses as bold capital text on each card, for example SUBMITTED. The coloured badges in this guide are only a reading aid and are not shown in the system itself.

Status reference across all modules
StatusPTWTBMChecklistCCPWhat it means / what to do
NEW✓✓✓✓Form open, nothing saved yet. Submit or lose it.
SUBMITTED✓✓✓✓Waiting for the first reviewer. Check Pending.
ASSESSED✓PTW only: waiting for HEA Safety.
VERIFIED✓PTW only: waiting for Project Manager approval.
APPROVED✓✓✓(chart only)Accepted. For PTW, work may start and daily reviews apply.
COMPLETED✓CCP approved. The Overview chart shows this as "Approved".
CLOSED✓PTW work declared complete; awaiting or past closure review.
RETURNED✓✓✓✓Sent back with a reason. The creator fixes it and resubmits.
REJECTED✓✓✓✓Refused permanently. Raise a new record.
REVOKED✓Approved PTW cancelled. Stop work.
DELETED✓CCP withdrawn by its creator after a return.

A–Z glossary
Applicant
The person who raises a record. Also the name of the basic role bundle.
Approver
A reviewer. Also the name of the reviewer role bundle.
Attachment
A photo or PDF (max 4 MB) added as evidence.
Building Name
The unique identifier of a lift or escalator location in the Equipment List. The Select Team screen also (confusingly) uses this label for the team name.
CAPTCHA
The number code on the sign-in page.
CCP
Compliance Confirmation Point (formerly "Compliance Check Point").
Change Team
Menu item that returns you to the team list.
CKL
Short for the Safety Action Key Points Checklist.
Closure Review
PTW Part 7: the main contractor's acknowledgement that the work is complete.
Company Admin
Administrator limited to their own company's users.
Configuration panel
The right-hand menu holding the setup screens.
Contractor / Constructor
A company: HEA or a subcontractor. The code says "Constructor"; the screens mostly say "Contractor".
CSOC
Construction Safety Orientation Course, the mandatory Singapore safety induction mentioned in the PTW conditions.
Daily Review
PTW Part 5: a daily tick by the applicant and an assessor.
Designation
Job title (the "Position" field on the user account).
EL / ES
Elevator (lift) / Escalator.
Endorsement
An approver's sign-off block.
Equipment
A lift or escalator unit belonging to a team.
HEA
Hitachi Elevator Asia.
Key Activities
The activity a CCP confirms, for example "Hoisting of lift cage".
Machine Type
Elevator or Escalator. It selects the checklist template.
Main contractor
The company that owns a team. Its staff get wider PTW visibility.
Manpower at Site
Daily headcount derived from Toolbox Meeting attendance.
MFG No. / Manufacturing Number
The unit's manufacturing serial.
Not applicable
Checklist option that excludes a whole section.
Pending
The list of records waiting for you to act.
PPE
Personal Protective Equipment.
Project
Older word for Team.
PTW
Permit To Work.
Return
Send back for correction (not final).
Reject
Refuse permanently.
Revoke
Cancel an approved PTW.
Session (AM/PM)
Morning or afternoon TBM.
SHMS / SWP
HEA's Safety & Health Management System / Safe Work Practices.
TBM
Toolbox Meeting.
TBM Approver
The one person per team who endorses that team's TBMs.
Team
The work group or site all records are filed under.
Template
A predefined list of checklist questions (per PTW work type, CCP activity, TBM, or elevator/escalator checklist).
UAT
User Acceptance Testing: the trial environment.
User ID
Your email address.
WAH
Working At Height.
WSH
Workplace Safety and Health (Singapore Act).

Troubleshooting & FAQ

Day-to-day problems and their usual fixes. Start with the quick checklist, then find your symptom below.

Quick checklist before calling for help
  1. Is the right team selected? The team name is in the page header (for example "Overview (Team M1)"). Use Change Team if not.
  2. Did you open the page from the menu? Lists are only refreshed when you re-open them from the menu.
  3. Is there a red message next to a field or under the title? Read it. The tables in each module tab explain every message.
  4. Did you allow location in the browser?
  5. Is each attachment under 4 MB and a .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .png or .pdf file?
  6. Has your session expired? If you were sent to the sign-in page, sign in again. Unsubmitted work is lost.
"I can't find the team I need."

You only see teams owned by your company or teams you've been added to as staff. Ask an administrator to add you in Project Configuration → 2. Manpower & Staff. If the team was renamed, look for the new name. If it was deleted, it no longer appears.

"The equipment / Manufacturing Number / Building Name dropdown is empty or missing a unit."

Only active equipment of the selected team appears. Ask an administrator to check Equipment List for that team. The unit may be locked, deleted or registered under another team.

"I can't submit my Toolbox Meeting: it says the team needs an active TBM approver."

The team has no approver, or the approver's account is inactive, has no email, or lacks the Approver bundle. An administrator must open Team Management, edit the team, and choose a valid TBM Approver. Also check that the team isn't locked.

"My approver says they never got an email."

Only Toolbox Meetings send an email ("TBM awaiting approval"), and only to the team's named TBM approver. PTW, Checklist and CCP send no emails, so approvers must check Pending.

Emails are sent by a separate HEA mail service, not by this application. If TBM emails stop arriving, ask IT to check that service and the approver's email address.

"A record isn't in my Pending list."
  • Re-open Pending from the menu to refresh it.
  • PTW: each stage appears only to its role: Assessor → Safety → Approver. The Approver stage and approved permits are shown only to main-contractor staff.
  • TBM: only the team's named approver (or an Admin) sees it.
  • CCP: you need the CCP APPROVER role, which comes with the Approver bundle.
  • Check that you have the right team selected.
"I clicked Submit / Approve and nothing happened."

First scroll the whole form for red messages. If there are none, a save error may have occurred. The PTW, CCP and Checklist screens hide these errors. Note the module, team, date, time and what you clicked, and report it to the system administrator. Don't keep clicking: check the list first to see whether the record was saved.

"I opened 'New' but it shows an old record."

The form remembers the last record you viewed if it is opened without the menu (for example with the browser Back button). Always start a new record from the left-menu "New" item.

"My PTW dates are rejected."

The start date must be today or later, the end date must not be before the start date, and the period can be at most 7 days. When resubmitting a returned permit whose start date has passed, move the dates forward.

"I can't tick yesterday's / last week's daily review."

Each day's Verify only works on that day or the next. Older days are closed by design. Record the reason in the next day's remarks.

"My checklist ticks disappeared."

Adding or removing equipment rebuilds the checklist and clears every tick. Add all units first, then tick.

"The new user didn't get their password."

Check the email address in User Management, then click Reset Password to send a new one. Ask the user to check their junk folder for an email titled "Reset Password".

"Someone has two accounts."

This happens when an admin changes a user's email address: the system creates a new account instead of renaming. Delete the old account.

"The manpower chart looks too low."

Manpower is counted only from submitted or approved Toolbox Meetings. Workers not added as attendees, and teams that skipped their TBM, are not counted. Each AM or PM session counts as half a person-day.

"The CCP Monitoring report shows other teams' buildings."

This is expected. The report covers all teams regardless of which team is selected. Use the column filters or grouping to narrow it.

Daily routine checklist for each role
RoleDaily routine
Team leader (Applicant)Submit the TBM before work. Submit a Checklist per job. Raise a PTW at least 3 working days ahead. Tick the PTW daily review. Record a CCP at key activities. Complete permits when the work is done. Check the lists for RETURNED items.
Assessor / Safety / Project ManagerCheck PTW Pending at least twice a day. Do the assessor daily reviews. Check Checklist Pending and CCP Pending Approval.
Team TBM approverAct on "TBM awaiting approval" emails the same day.
AdministratorOnboard and remove users. Keep equipment lists current. Make sure every team has a valid TBM approver ("Not assigned" in Team Management means TBMs are blocked).
ManagementReview the Overview charts per team. Export the TBM Report and CCP Monitoring monthly.

Known issues, gaps & handover notes

These were found by reading the source code and database scripts. They are written in plain English so you can prioritise them with a future developer or vendor. High means it affects safety records or security, Medium means it causes wrong data or user confusion, and Low is cosmetic.

Deployment state (read first)
  • The latest changes (late September 2026) were built and tested only on the previous developer's own PC. According to their handover note, they have not yet been deployed to the UAT system, and the database update scripts have not been run on UAT. Those changes include the TBM hazard fields, the TBM approver rules, the CCP and checklist name fields, equipment delete and the CCP report fixes.
  • The database update scripts are in the Database folder of the code repository, named by date. Two files starting with DONTRUN_ must not be run.
  • The developer's PC configuration includes a sign-in shortcut that skips the CAPTCHA. Their note says this setting must not be copied to UAT or production.
  • The menu wording and which roles see which menu items live in the database, not in the code. They need checking on the live system with an admin login and a normal user login.
Security and access
SeverityIssueImpact
HighPasswords are stored as readable text (not encrypted) and limited to 20 characters. There are no complexity rules and no lockout after failed attempts.Anyone with database access can read every password.
HighPages are not protected by role, only by sign-in. Anyone signed in who knows a page's address can open it, including settings pages and the hidden Document List.Hiding a menu item does not prevent access.
HighA non-admin editing their own account in User Management can change their own role bundle to Admin.Users can give themselves admin rights.

MediumSelf-approval is not blocked for PTW, Checklist or CCP (only for TBM).One person could approve their own safety record.
MediumSessions last up to 60 hours.A shared or unattended device stays signed in.

  • Source code repository: github.com/dcshengzz/HEA-EPTW-MTE.
  • Full database structure as of 16 Sep 2026: EPTW-MTE-UAT-backup.txt. Later changes: Database/2026*.sql, to be run in date order and skipping DONTRUN_*.
